newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ex-MOF official says G7 to tolerate weak yen - Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Ex-MOF official says G7 to tolerate weak yen - Jiji.

text.p: Finance ministers from the Group of Seven (G7) industrial nations will likely agree to tolerate the dollar's recent rise against the yen at their meeting in Berlin on Saturday, Jiji news agency quoted a former Japanese Finance Ministry official as saying on Monday.

Makoto Utsumi, a former vice finance minister for international affairs, told Jiji that a statement expected to be issued after the G7 meeting may include expressions which would endorse recent moves in foreign exchange markets.

"The expression used in the statement on currencies may be one that endorses the current situation," Utsumi was quoted as saying in Davos, Switzerland, where he is attending an annual meeting of the World Economic Forum.
He added that the G7 officials are likely to agree to pursue exchange rate stability while allowing the dollar to remain at current levels against the yen.

Jiji quoted Utsumi as saying that it would be difficult to imagine the G7 nations agreeing on something that may lead to a sharp correction in the strength of the dollar against the yen, or on something that would add momentum to the rise of the dollar.
Rather, the G7 countries are expected to observe that the current exchange rate levels are in line with economic fundamentals, Utsumi was quoted as saying.

Utsumi, now a professor at Japan's private Keio University, suggested that the G7 countries have in mind a target range of 105 to 120 yen to the dollar for now, noting that Germany does not welcome a further rise in the dollar, Jiji said.
U.S. manufacturers are also concerned about Washington's hands-off attitude towards the dollar's surge, Utsumi was quoted as saying.
He added that the dollar at 120 yen should not hurt the Japanese economy or its manufacturers.
